request: Build a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open that runs on NVIDIA DGX Spark. The attached System Ontology files describe the model, the machine, the target the engine is judged on, and the engine itself at two levels: the system as a whole and its nodes. Take them as the statement of what is wanted.

documents.name: target.yaml
documents.text:
kind: engine_spec
id: spec/muse-spark-open-on-dgx-spark/target
title: "First use case: a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA DGX Spark"
spec_level: target
ontology_version: 0.6.1
# What the scope page states is written with its source. What the scope page leaves undefined but an engine cannot be
# judged without is written as a proposal (status: proposed) so that it can be confirmed or replaced. What only the
# project can decide stays UNSET. Fields left to the factory are `open`.
# On 2026-11-19 the bench owner answered what the bench runs now. Those answers are written as proposals with that
# source: they say what is measured today, not what the project requires. Three things this file had written did
# not match the kickoff page or the bench's practice and were corrected: the baseline, the memory budget and the
# checkpoint.

given:
  model: model/muse-spark-open-ud-iq2-xxs   # the files the bench has run since 2026-11-16: a third party's conversion at about 2 bits per expert weight. The project has not confirmed it in writing. The model as published is model/muse-spark-open.
  hardware: hw/dgx-spark
  environment: env/dgx-spark-measured-20261119   # measured on the DGX Spark itself on 2026-11-19 (tools/spark_kit/probe.py)

boundary:
  form: {value: service, status: proposed, source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19: the baseline is an online service with an OpenAI-compatible interface"}
  packaging: {value: container, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}

interface:
  input:  {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  output: {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  streaming: UNSET               # bench: not fixed in its configuration; whether first-token latency is measured on a stream was not verified

execution: open
state: open
composition: open
policy: open
binding: open

contract:
  requirements:
    - id: c-mem
      quantity: memory_budget
      kind: pass_fail
      unit: GB
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "Everything the engine's container holds in the unified pool at any moment: allocations of the process on CPU and GPU, and page cache attributable to the files it reads. The operating system and other processes are outside."
      candidates:
        - {value: 128, unit: GB, unit_basis: decimal, pool: mem0, source: "kickoff page: the target, a working set of 128 GB of unified memory"}
        - {value: 80, unit: GB, unit_basis: decimal, pool: mem0, source: "kickoff page: the reference configuration of Strata on DGX Spark, 80 GB of unified memory"}
      source: "kickoff page; bench owner, 2026-11-19"
      note: "The kickoff page names three figures. Its target is a working set of 128 GB of unified memory. 80 GB is the reference configuration of Strata on this machine. 12 GB is a feasibility target, which the bench proposes to read as the GPU working set. Until 2026-11-19 this file took 80 GB as the budget; the bench owner pointed out that this does not match the page. The machine reports 130.6 GB in all and about 127 GB allocatable, so a budget of 128 GB as written is more than it can give. What the bench measured for its baseline: a GPU working set of 21.6 GiB, and a peak resident size of about 107 GiB, most of it the mapped weight files. Which figure is the budget, and by which accounting, is the project's to say."
    - id: c-context
      quantity: context_length
      kind: pass_fail
      value: UNSET
      unit: tokens
      note: "The model allows about 1,000,000 tokens. The attention state for the offered context is taken from the same memory as the expert cache. The bench starts its server with a context of 20,480 tokens and has tested prompts of about 16,000 tokens with 128 output tokens; it says this is its own setting and not a requirement on the engine (bench owner, 2026-11-19)."
    - id: c-quality
      quantity: quality_score
      kind: pass_fail
      status: proposed
      baseline: "llama.cpp with the Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS conversion (about 226 GB, pinned by hash), the published tokenizer, temperature 0 (greedy), seed 1234. Set on 2026-11-16."
      comparison: "The bench's tool can compare in two ways: a task score that drops by no more than the noise between two runs of the same configuration, and token probabilities by top-1 agreement and KL divergence with a lowest agreement that can be set. It does not compare token by token for identity. Which rule decides a pass is not set."
      taskset: "GSM8K (5-shot, 50 questions, at most 256 output tokens); RULER niah_single_2 and qa_hotpot at 4K and 16K; a determinism test (3 questions, 3 runs each, 64 tokens); token probabilities (20 prompts, 64 tokens each)."
      threshold: UNSET           # the bench records scores (GSM8K 0.94) and has no pass threshold
      source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19. Until then this file named the published reference implementation with the NVFP4 weights as the baseline, which is not what is run."
    - id: c-ttft
      quantity: ttft
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      timing_start: "The engine admits the request. Model load is excluded."
      timing_end: "The first output token is produced by the engine."
      workload: "Speed: a prompt of about 2,000 tokens after 0, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens of earlier context, 128 output tokens; one request at a time; new prompts only (prompt cache off; the measured share of reused prefix is 0.8%); up to 6 warm-up requests, discarded."
      source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19"
      note: "The bench records two figures: one timed by the client and one timed by the engine, which is this definition. Model load is recorded apart. Cold start is recorded apart as well: the first request is 2.44 times slower, and the server is ready 132 s after start."
    - id: c-decode
      quantity: decode_rate
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      includes_first_token: false
      workload: "Speed: a prompt of about 2,000 tokens after 0, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens of earlier context, 128 output tokens; one request at a time; new prompts only (prompt cache off; the measured share of reused prefix is 0.8%); up to 6 warm-up requests, discarded."
      source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19"
      note: "The bench takes the engine's own timing, apart from the prompt. Whether the first token is counted in it was not checked in the runtime's source."
    - id: c-peak
      quantity: peak_memory
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "The same boundary as c-mem."
      workload: "The peak over every phase of the whole bench run, not a load of its own."
      source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19"
      note: "What the bench records: the GPU working set (21.6 GiB), the process's resident size per phase (highest about 107 GiB, most of it mapped weight files, split into anonymous, shared and file-mapped), and the lowest available memory of the machine. Not covered: figures at container level (the baseline does not run in a container) and page cache that the process has not mapped. Its unit is GiB. The figure this requirement defines has not been computed."
  allowed_transformations: UNSET # the baseline itself is already below NVFP4 (about 2 bits). What an engine may change relative to that baseline is not set: the comparison rule of c-quality is open
  workload: {value: "Fixed values, not distributions. Speed: a prompt of about 2,000 tokens after 0, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens of earlier context, 128 output tokens; one request at a time; new prompts only (prompt cache off; the measured share of reused prefix is 0.8%); up to 6 warm-up requests, discarded. No workload with several turns of one conversation. Quality: the task set of c-quality.", status: proposed, source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19"}

delivery:
  model_checkpoint: {value: "Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B, Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS conversion to GGUF: six files, 225.6 GB, pinned by hash", status: proposed, source: "bench owner, 2026-11-19: what the bench has run since 2026-11-16"}
  deliverables:
    - {item: reproducible_container, resolution: required}
    - {item: clean_rebuild,          resolution: required}
    - {item: benchmark_report,       resolution: required}
    - {item: replayable_run_artifacts, resolution: required}

documents.text:
# Generated by tools/so_derive.py from _derive.yaml. Edit that file, not this one.
kind: system
id: sys/muse-on-spark
title: Engine for Muse Spark Open on DGX Spark (proposed)
summary: A proposed engine for a mixture-of-experts model whose expert weights are about three times the machine's memory.
  Each token uses 8 of 256 experts in each of 62 layers. The weights every token needs stay in memory. All experts stay
  on storage in a file prepared so that one expert is one contiguous read. A cache in memory holds the most used experts;
  a routed expert that is not cached is read from storage for that step and may replace a less used one. Reading is started
  as soon as routing is known and overlaps with the computation of the experts already in memory. The design is taken from
  Strata component by component, with the storage path taken from ds4, and nothing of it has been built.
product:
  name: Muse engine (working name)
  form: A design derived from the descriptions of Strata and ds4. No implementation exists.
targets:
- model: model/muse-spark-open-ud-iq2-xxs
  hardware: hw/dgx-spark
  input_modalities:
  - text
  note: Text in, text out. The perception encoder for image, video and audio is not loaded in the first version.
mechanisms:
- mech/hot-expert-residency
uncatalogued_mechanisms:
- family: read-latency-hidden-behind-compute
  summary: Start the storage read of a missed expert as soon as routing is known, and compute the cached experts of the
    same layer while it arrives.
- family: one-expert-one-read
  summary: Prepare the weight file offline so that each expert is one contiguous, block-aligned range, readable without
    parsing.
- family: layer-major-prompt-reading
  summary: Read a prompt chunk one layer at a time, so that an expert routed by many tokens of the chunk is read from storage
    once.
resource_expectations:
- holding: 'Weights every token uses: attention, router, embedding table, output head'
  held_on: fast_memory
  amount:
    value: 19.6
    unit: GB
    unit_basis: decimal
    status: measured
    source: 'model/muse-spark-open-ud-iq2-xxs: shared_weights 17.31 GB, token_embedding 0.93 GB, output_head_weights 1.36
      GB'
    note: As stored in the model files the bench runs, at 4.5 to 8 bits. At the 4 bits of the published weights these 21.1B
      parameters would take 10.6 GB.
- holding: Attention keys and values for the configured context length
  held_on: fast_memory
  amount: UNSET
  note: '0.254 MB per token at 16 bits when every layer keeps every token: 8.3 GB at 32,768 tokens. 46 of the 62 layers
    attend only to the last 2,048 tokens; an engine that keeps no more than that for them needs 2.5 GB at 32,768 tokens.
    The amount is open because the context length is.'
- holding: 'Expert cache: what remains of the memory budget'
  held_on: fast_memory
  note: 12.98 MB per expert in the model files the bench runs, so each GB holds about 77 experts of 15,872. At the 4 bits
    of the published weights an expert is 25.17 MB.
- holding: Every expert
  held_on: storage
  amount:
    value: 205.96
    unit: GB
    unit_basis: decimal
    status: measured
    source: model/muse-spark-open-ud-iq2-xxs, expert_weights
    note: 399.43 GB at the 4 bits of the published weights.
claims: []
components:
- comp/muse/preparation
- comp/muse/setup
- comp/muse/loading
- comp/muse/serving
- comp/muse/conversation-reuse
- comp/muse/prompt-path
- comp/muse/token-path
- comp/muse/expert-subsystem
- comp/muse/telemetry
declares:
  stages:
  - load
  - prefill
  - decode
  states:
  - attention_kv
  - expert_heat
  - residency_table
  - staged_experts
  - expert_usage_profile
  - admission_counters
  - prompt_encode_cache
  - engine_process_state
  - live_conversation_record
  - parked_conversations
  - run_config
  - dispatch_counts
  - run_manifest_record
  - request_history
  policies:
  - expert-cache
  - conversation-resume
  - parked-eviction
flows:
- id: model-geometry
  sender: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Layer count, widths, expert count and experts per token read from the metadata of the prepared files and
    checked against the compiled shapes; every later size is computed from it.
- id: expert-layout-file
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-layout
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'The table of expert ranges in the prepared files: for each expert, where its bytes lie and how long they
    are.'
- id: expert-layout-to-source
  sender: comp/muse/expert-layout
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: For each expert, the offset and length of its range in the prepared file, and the total bytes.
- id: expert-layout-to-sizing
  sender: comp/muse/expert-layout
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The largest expert range, the unit the expert cache's slots are counted in.
- id: shared-weights-read
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/weight-loader
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - shared_weights
  timing: startup
  description: The weights every token uses, read from the prepared files.
- id: shared-weights-in-memory
  sender: comp/muse/weight-loader
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - shared_weights
  timing: startup
  description: Where the weights every token uses lie in memory, by name.
- id: operator-memory-settings
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'Command-line flags and environment: context length, expert cache size or auto, reserve, prompt chunk.'
- id: free-memory
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: startup
  description: Free memory of the machine's one memory pool as the operating system reports it, read before the cache is
    sized and again after its slots are written.
- id: expert-cache-size
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Number of slots and the byte size of a slot.
- id: expert-bytes-from-files
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: The bytes of a requested expert, one contiguous range of the prepared file, read from storage when asked
    for.
- id: expert-ranges-to-read
  sender: comp/muse/expert-source
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: 'The ranges of the prepared file to be read: cache fill, replacements, the prompt path''s staging.'
- id: residency-lookup
  sender: comp/muse/expert-cache
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - residency_table
  timing: per_layer
  description: For each routed expert, the fast-memory slot holding it or that it is absent
- id: accelerator-expert-plan
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: plan
    refs:
    - expert_ffn
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which routed experts are computed this layer, from cache slots or from the staging area.
- id: step-fetch-request
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: per_layer
  description: Missed experts to read into the staging area for this step only.
- id: expert-usage
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/cache-policy
  carries:
    content: signal
    refs:
    - expert_heat
  timing: per_layer
  description: How many tokens of the step or of the prompt chunk routed each expert.
- id: swap-requests
  sender: comp/muse/cache-policy
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: background
  description: Experts to read into the slots of experts that are leaving the cache.
- id: residency-updates
  sender: comp/muse/cache-policy
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - residency_table
  timing: background
  description: A leaving expert is marked absent before its slot is overwritten; an entering expert is marked resident after
    its bytes have fully arrived.
- id: prompt-state
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-path
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_request
  description: The model state left by reading the prompt, from which generation continues
- id: step-inputs
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: The token id and its position for this step.
- id: routed-experts
  sender: comp/muse/expert-router
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: 8 expert ids and weights per token, read by the combine of expert rows.
- id: layer-handoff
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: 'When a layer''s routing is known: its feed-forward input and routed ids, handed to expert dispatch.'
- id: kv-pages-for-attention
  sender: comp/muse/kv-store
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_layer
  description: The keys and values an attention step reads.
- id: kv-append
  sender: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_layer
  description: The new position's keys and values of each attention layer, written into the store.
- id: final-residual-to-head
  sender: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  receiver: comp/muse/output-head
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_step
  description: The residual after the last layer, one per position.
- id: logits-to-sampler
  sender: comp/muse/output-head
  receiver: comp/muse/sampler
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_step
  description: One row of vocabulary logits per position.
- id: client-request
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: request
  timing: per_request
  description: 'A client request over HTTP: messages, sampling fields and an output limit.'
- id: client-response
  sender: comp/muse/http-front
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: response
  timing: per_step
  description: 'The response to the client: tokens as they are produced or one body at the end, with usage and timings.'
- id: messages-to-prompt
  sender: comp/muse/http-front
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  carries:
    content: request
  timing: per_request
  description: Messages and template arguments in one internal form.
- id: prompt-ids
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  receiver: comp/muse/request-runner
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: The prompt token ids and the output limit fitted to the context.
- id: generation-call
  sender: comp/muse/request-runner
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: Prompt token ids, output limit, sampling settings and a cancel event for one engine generation.
- id: engine-commands
  sender: comp/muse/engine-client
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: 'Text lines on the engine''s standard input: generate with settings and prompt token ids, stop, report memory,
    save and restore.'
- id: engine-token-lines
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: One line per produced token id.
- id: engine-stat-lines
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/server-metrics
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: per_request
  description: A line at start; per request, prompt progress, a line when a conversation is resumed, and an end line with
    counts, prompt and decode milliseconds, reused tokens and expert cache hits.
- id: tokens-to-runner
  sender: comp/muse/engine-client
  receiver: comp/muse/request-runner
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: Token ids as they arrive, with a heartbeat after a set time of quiet.
- id: response-events
  sender: comp/muse/request-runner
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: response
  timing: per_step
  description: Content events, pings and one finish record.
- id: prompt-to-read
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: The prompt token ids of one generation, to be read from the resume point.
- id: resume-point
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: per_request
  description: How many prompt tokens the session already holds, so reading starts there
- id: take-or-park
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: Park the outgoing conversation; restore from the chosen parked entry.
- id: parked-restore
  sender: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: A parked conversation's attention keys and values and its token record, copied back into the live conversation.
- id: session-file-out
  sender: comp/muse/session-files
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: 'One session file on storage: the conversation''s token record and every attention layer''s keys and values.'
- id: session-file-in
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/session-files
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: A session file read back and validated before the live state is written.
- id: operator-choices
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: offline
  description: 'The person''s setup answers and options: model, context length, format of the attention state, reserve.'
- id: run-config
  sender: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  receiver: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'The run configuration file: engine path, argument list, environment, the person''s own options and server
    keys'
- id: engine-argv
  sender: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The engine process's argument list and environment
- id: memory-options
  sender: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Context length, format of the attention state, memory reserve and expert cache request, as engine arguments.
- id: request-figures
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: per_request
  description: Usage with cached tokens and the timings object placed in the response
- id: metrics-out
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: on_demand
  description: The records, totals and rates, rendered for outside monitors when they ask.
- id: hardware-readings
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/server-metrics
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: background
  description: GPU utilisation, temperature and power from the vendor library, and CPU, memory and disk readings from the
    operating system.
- id: gpu-busy
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: background
  description: Whether the GPU is working, read by the frozen-engine check.
- id: diagnostic-files
  sender: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: on_demand
  description: The counts report at exit and the run manifest, each only when asked for.
- id: published-checkpoint
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/preparation
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
    - shared_weights
  timing: offline
  description: The published checkpoint, read once
- id: prepared-files
  sender: comp/muse/preparation
  receiver: model_files
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
    - shared_weights
  timing: offline
  description: 'The files the engine reads: weights every token uses, and every expert as one range'
- id: prepared-header
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Metadata and tensor directory of the prepared files
- id: head-weights
  sender: comp/muse/weight-loader
  receiver: comp/muse/output-head
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - output_head_weights
  timing: startup
  description: Where the output head's weights lie in fast memory
- id: context-plan
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The context length the attention state is sized for
- id: chunk-plan
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The chunk size and the memory the prompt path may use
- id: read-requests
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: Which experts to deliver and into which buffers
- id: staged-experts-ready
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - staged_experts
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which missed experts of this layer have arrived
- id: fetched-experts-to-cache
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: The bytes of an expert the cache policy admitted
- id: prompt-layer-handoff
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-path
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: For one layer of one chunk, the routing of every token and the activations
- id: generate
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/decode-loop
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: Start generating from the current attention state, with the sampling settings and the token limit
- id: picked-token
  sender: comp/muse/sampler
  receiver: comp/muse/decode-loop
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: The token chosen for this step; it is the input of the next
- id: emitted-tokens
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: Each generated token as it is produced
- id: truncate-to-prefix
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_request
  description: Cut the attention state back to the shared prefix
- id: routing-counts
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  carries:
    content: signal
    refs:
    - expert_usage_profile
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which experts were routed, and which were found in the cache
- id: usage-profile-out
  sender: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
    refs:
    - expert_usage_profile
  timing: on_demand
  description: The recorded usage of every expert, written as a file that a later start can load
derived_from:
- system: sys/strata
  consulted_for: 'The decomposition as a whole: loading, serving, conversation reuse, the per-token path, the expert subsystem
    and telemetry.'
  main_source: true
  not_carried:
  - component: comp/strata/native-weight-loader
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It serves tensors Strata keeps in GGUF form. Muse's prepared files have one form and one loader.
  - component: comp/strata/host-memory-admission
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It admits a page-locked host copy of every expert and of the lookup table. Muse's experts are three times the
      machine's memory and the model has no lookup table.
  - component: comp/strata/slot-scheduler
    why: postponed
    note: A second conversation needs its own attention state in memory, taken from the expert cache.
  - component: comp/strata/replica-router
    why: does_not_apply
    note: 'One machine: there is no second engine to route a request to.'
  - component: comp/strata/checkpoint-chain
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It exists to go back in recurrent state that cannot be truncated. Muse's card names attention state only.
  - component: comp/strata/speed-calibration
    why: postponed
    note: Its presets were measured on Strata's weight packs. It needs first measurements of this engine.
  - component: comp/strata/mtp-drafter
    why: does_not_apply
    note: The model card names no draft head.
  - component: comp/strata/dflash2-drafter
    why: does_not_apply
    note: A separate drafter model trained for Strata's model.
  - component: comp/strata/lookup-drafter
    why: postponed
    note: It needs nothing from the model, but a window of drafted tokens routes more experts per step. Whether that pays
      depends on the cost of a miss and on the acceptance rate, neither measured.
  - component: comp/strata/draft-policy
    why: postponed
    note: Postponed with the lookup drafter.
  - component: comp/strata/draft-verifier
    why: postponed
    note: Postponed with the lookup drafter.
  - component: comp/strata/session-loop
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It exists for one of Strata's weight packs only.
  - component: comp/strata/window-graphs
    why: postponed
    note: Replaying one recorded graph per step assumes no wait inside a layer. Here a layer may wait for storage. To be
      revisited when the miss rate is measured.
  - component: comp/strata/ngram-reader
    why: does_not_apply
    note: The model card names no lookup table.
  - component: comp/strata/cpu-expert-pool
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It computes experts the GPU cannot reach. On one memory pool the GPU reads every expert that is in memory, and
      an expert that is not in memory is on storage, where the CPU has no advantage.
- system: sys/ds4
  consulted_for: 'The storage path: offline preparation of the weight file, reading experts from storage on demand, eviction.'
  main_source: false
coverage: 'A design, not a description of something built. Each component names the existing component it was adapted from.
  Every text here comes from one of two places: it was written for this engine in the derivation list, or it is the source''s
  text and the derivation''s list of kept texts names it as read against this engine, with the reason. The derivation writes
  no other text of the source and changes none by itself. Of a source component an adapted component also takes the title,
  the role, the timings, the state and the names of what it performs, without the names this engine does not have. The kept
  texts were read by Claude, an AI model, and not by a person. Word patterns for the source model''s numbers and features,
  the source machine''s kinds of memory, the source engine''s name and implementation identifiers are looked for in every
  text; they find the usual wordings and nothing else. Not covered in the first version: image, video and audio input; drafting;
  generating more than one conversation at the same time; more than one machine. The state of earlier conversations may
  be kept for reuse, within a memory budget that may be zero.'

documents.name: nodes.yaml
documents.text:
# The node level of Engine for Muse Spark Open on DGX Spark (proposed) under the generic node types. Written by
# `tools/so_nodetypes.py example muse-on-spark`. The type of each node is the one stated in node-assignment.yaml
# beside this file, read from the component's own text and pinned to its responsibility
# (`responsibility_sha256`); `fit` and `reason` appear where that reading found the type does not fit plainly.
# `settles` names the choices of the type this design decides, with its decisions word for word, from
# validation/choices/map-muse-on-spark.yaml, keyed by decision id and text. `own_decisions` counts the
# decisions of the component that are not a kept choice of its types. The full description of each
# component is at `described_in`.
engine: muse-on-spark
node_types: ontology/node-types.draft.yaml, draft 0.9
nodes:
- component: preparation
  title: Model preparation
  described_in: comp/muse/preparation
  derived_from:
  - comp/ds4/model-preparation
  type: model-conversion
  responsibility_sha256: 49b5c464d2dfa82009b6cfbed6db268cf73d6a51ef6f861aa2054c0e91073096
  does: 'Offline, turn the published checkpoint into the files the engine reads: the weights every token uses in load order,
    and every expert as one contiguous block-aligned range with a table of where each lies.'
- component: model-file-reader
  title: Model file reader and geometry check
  described_in: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/model-file-reader
  type: model-loading
  responsibility_sha256: 6e9c84607b6ab89eb422b7673ab526185a9cf7594908d85910fa3e1cf40076bf
  does: Open the prepared files read-only, expose their metadata and tensor directory unchanged, and refuse files whose
    declared shape the compiled kernels cannot run.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: expert-layout
  title: Expert layout table
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-layout
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-layout
  type: model-loading
  responsibility_sha256: e921ff03fc1b05cf367627bb48460ee4645fe21abe4c150211857ea98e4963f5
  does: Read the table of expert ranges once and answer, for the whole process, where each expert's bytes lie in the prepared
    file and how long they are.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: weight-loader
  title: Weight loader
  described_in: comp/muse/weight-loader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/weight-loader
  type: model-loading
  responsibility_sha256: 4e5d0f4c2473eb45d96f053f6b78dfabcc5323b544246754d47013368af4291c
  does: At startup, place the weights every token uses in fast memory and return a table from tensor name to location.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: startup-memory-sizing
  title: Startup memory sizing
  described_in: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/startup-memory-sizing
  type: memory-planning
  responsibility_sha256: ab6b10ecc8a81a9af982f9218313377da8fee7847e9d29c3e1ff67ece8f69bb4
  does: Within the memory budget, price the weights every token uses, the attention state for the configured context, the
    staging area and a reserve; give the expert cache what remains; and refuse to start when the cache would be below its
    minimum.
  settles:
  - choice: the reserve left free
    how:
    - Memory left free for the operating system and for allocations not priced in advance.
  - choice: the least a cache may be and still work
    how:
    - 'The smallest cache the engine will start with: at least the experts one step can route, 8 times 62.'
  own_decisions: 3
- component: layer-kernels
  title: Layer kernels and their order
  described_in: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/layer-kernels
  type: layer-compute
  responsibility_sha256: b7bf4fa72d8cdd4cdea796c413843c52b7e12f1a58864db64edb40381d4dc206
  does: Compute the part of each layer every token needs, in a fixed order.
- component: expert-router
  title: Expert router
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-router
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-router
  type: layer-compute
  responsibility_sha256: fa16b7600b22e8ad1d515a7639ee5ab2c5a285cf7131701b22bbe6630ca89dc3
  does: For each token in each layer, turn the feed-forward input into 256 logits and choose 8 experts with their weights.
- component: output-head
  title: Output head
  described_in: comp/muse/output-head
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/output-head
  type: layer-compute
  responsibility_sha256: 5346ca133861d9b961f89dab3324f1748028dbbccbdaac773903eed2154b86c9
  does: Turn the residual after the last layer into one row of vocabulary logits per position.
- component: decode-loop
  title: Decode loop
  described_in: comp/muse/decode-loop
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/window-loop
  - comp/ds4/decode-loop
  type: step-execution
  responsibility_sha256: 4ec78b0249867dafbc0568d0f7598e81590826db79c1c624b55a8c3981b44b4b
  does: Take one token through the 62 layers and the output head, at each layer handing the routing to the expert subsystem
    and waiting until every routed expert has been computed.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: prompt-path
  title: Prompt path
  described_in: comp/muse/prompt-path
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/prompt-path
  - comp/ds4/prefill-driver
  type: prompt-reading
  responsibility_sha256: 1f046f08c90b41472f6db985131d67895c364522a25f5912bf3f2099dfa3fc50
  does: Read the prompt in chunks, one layer at a time, reading each routed expert that is not cached once per chunk, and
    leave behind the attention state that generation continues from.
  settles:
  - choice: chunk size
    how:
    - Tokens per chunk. Larger chunks amortise each expert read over more tokens but need more experts in memory at once.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: expert-source
  title: Expert source
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-source
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-source
  - comp/ds4/expert-stream-reader
  type: expert-source
  responsibility_sha256: e3465b213550b638f5217459c0c1db7e9875ae78cdfd4149ad99ab1cba92a0f3
  does: For any expert, give the range of the prepared file that holds it, and deliver its bytes into a buffer it is handed.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: expert-cache
  title: Expert cache
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-cache
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-cache
  - comp/ds4/expert-cache
  type: expert-cache
  responsibility_sha256: ac575090e312fd8ae041be413d891d54e4af8689cda04c18f27dfb71d5fd1226
  does: Hold as many experts in fast memory as its budget allows and answer, for any expert, whether it is there and in
    which slot.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: cache-policy
  title: Cache policy
  described_in: comp/muse/cache-policy
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/adaptive-tier
  - comp/ds4/expert-eviction
  type: residency-policy
  responsibility_sha256: 3bc4e4cbe4aea7aa650cfb5d0a1a1e66de02ae4def4d5c2638672cb4e58b3f9b
  does: Decide, for an expert that has just been read from storage, whether it enters the cache and which resident expert
    leaves, so that the cache holds the experts the current work uses most.
  settles:
  - choice: how use counts age, so that recent use outweighs old use
    how:
    - How fast usage counts fade.
  own_decisions: 3
- component: storage-reader
  title: Storage reader
  described_in: comp/muse/storage-reader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/host-to-device-transfer
  - comp/ds4/expert-stream-reader
  type: expert-fetch
  responsibility_sha256: 8495daa3961301f1242ffc7c36634daa87fd9e49212b7f4b6e5851fa43f44c6e
  does: Read the bytes of missed experts from storage into the staging area or a cache slot, several at a time, and report
    each as ready only when it is complete.
- component: expert-dispatch
  title: Expert dispatch
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-dispatch
  - comp/ds4/expert-split-dispatch
  type: expert-dispatch
  also: [layer-compute]
  responsibility_sha256: 72c221532e5a9d20df0229e8eb734d5dfa23ffa78cea0ca0c5993349b1301e45
  does: For one layer of one step, decide for every routed expert whether it is computed from the cache at once or after
    a read from storage, and issue the reads before the cached experts start computing.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: kv-store
  title: Key and value store
  described_in: comp/muse/kv-store
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/kv-store
  type: positional-state-store
  responsibility_sha256: d0a7e52df469193ce9822213c17359338f73a6d0d1af6a119047bc5d272b26c6
  does: Hold the attention keys and values of every position up to the configured context length, and truncate them to a
    given position when asked.
- component: resume-decision
  title: Resume decision
  described_in: comp/muse/resume-decision
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/resume-decision
  type: prefix-reuse
  responsibility_sha256: f6eda388af1c280befb5d1f9ea9b6ba0a001dd6d9bfd1809eaa9448e4c0ba017
  does: For each request, choose the stored state that shares the longest valid prefix with the prompt, make the session
    hold exactly that state by truncating or restoring, and report the prefix length.
- component: parked-conversations
  title: Parked conversation cache
  described_in: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/parked-conversations
  type: prefix-reuse
  responsibility_sha256: 1876a97cfdc1bb2fa70c7b0b43f3716075b3d319987215f3caa66c4e5e00c602
  does: Hold images of other conversations' attention state within a budget, find the one with the longest valid prefix
    for a prompt, and evict.
- component: session-files
  title: Session files
  described_in: comp/muse/session-files
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/session-files
  type: session-persistence
  responsibility_sha256: 251cb049b28b9a79b23ba5c5f9f45a082c41dc5007e7c5136d92f267f86c4c32
  does: On an explicit command, write the session's current conversation to one file or read one back, refusing any file
    that does not belong to this model, configuration and engine version before any state changes.
- component: sampler
  title: Sampler
  described_in: comp/muse/sampler
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/sampler
  type: sampling
  responsibility_sha256: 8dc0c0ca7db8836f5138809b749625ab6a878b6dad5d50fc1cd30b2647562c64
  does: 'Turn the logits of the position being generated into one token id by a fixed chain: logit bias, penalties, top-k,
    top-p, min-p, temperature, pick.'
- component: request-runner
  title: Request runner
  described_in: comp/muse/request-runner
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/request-runner
  type: output-interpretation
  fit: partial
  reason: It also drives one API request through one or more engine generations, a job of the serving side that output-interpretation
    does not name and that no single type describes.
  responsibility_sha256: 771cf7fc82655449b38b6d91d1b38dfae3e87df7ce55f42675825a4829113ca1
  does: Drive one API request through one or more engine generations and turn the token ids into content events with a final
    finish record.
- component: http-front
  title: HTTP front and admission bound
  described_in: comp/muse/http-front
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/http-front
  type: request-front
  fit: partial
  reason: It also bounds how many inference calls are pending and owns the admission counters. request-front does not name
    admission, and no other type is that job at the door (resource-governing is about memory or power, sequence-lifecycle
    about sequences inside the engine).
  responsibility_sha256: 68f9e9c1d98a3f34da666bff581610a8806f059891121e8594d4011d483638cc
  does: Accept client requests over HTTP, bound how many inference calls are pending, answer every failure class with a
    defined status code, and cancel a request whose client has hung up.
- component: prompt-builder
  title: Prompt builder
  described_in: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/prompt-builder
  type: prompt-preparation
  responsibility_sha256: c19c100d6269549395f677dd7b41d367c2877c32309a492bde60a44160feb177
  does: Produce the exact prompt token ids and the token limit for a request from its messages, or refuse the request.
  settles:
  - choice: the template used and how it is corrected
    how:
    - The template that turns messages into one prompt.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: engine-client
  title: Engine process client and supervisor
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-client
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-client
  type: engine-supervision
  responsibility_sha256: d42f7c0d580fba81e41675f0f8397351a652f9a3bd4fda3c7d55cf92f6623202
  does: 'Keep one engine child process resident and in step with the server: send each generation as one text command, deliver
    its token lines to the caller, and end and restart a process that is dead, silent, frozen or fatally broken.'
- component: engine-command-loop
  title: Engine command loop
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-command-loop
  type: engine-supervision
  also: [sequence-lifecycle]
  fit: partial
  reason: 'The suggested main type, step-scheduler, does not fit its text: with one generation at a time nothing decides
    what a step contains or which sequences join it. Of sequence-lifecycle it has only the record; admitting, pausing and
    releasing sequences are not in its text.'
  responsibility_sha256: 68f97f43878fdbebfb1131007375aecec2fd6fdf1688577d65a84aa145fcd3cf
  does: Inside the engine process, read one command at a time, run one prompt read and one generation at a time, and report
    each generation's tokens and end figures as text lines.
- component: run-config-generator
  title: Run configuration generator and store
  described_in: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/run-config-generator
  type: configuration
  responsibility_sha256: a6a67fb45a2134d8e441ca0e556950c326966978835b28a4aa94a9292f43906c
  does: Produce a complete run configuration file for one model on this machine from machine facts and the person's answers,
    and rewrite it without losing what the person added by hand.
- component: launch-argument-resolver
  title: Launch and start-time argument resolver
  described_in: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/launch-argument-resolver
  type: configuration
  responsibility_sha256: 825b72c64f89f87038177560de0ba85c2afe67f4f5dad740e1febd04079e1a0c
  does: Turn the stored run configuration into the argument list and environment the engine process actually receives, at
    every launch and every engine start, so that standing choices kept outside the list cannot be undone by whoever last
    rewrote it.
- component: engine-diagnostics
  title: Engine diagnostics
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-diagnostics
  type: telemetry
  also: [calibration]
  fit: partial
  reason: The responsibility itself says only that the counts are recorded and written when asked, which is telemetry. That
    the usage profile is input other nodes take as fixed (calibration) rests on the system level (the flow usage-profile-out,
    'a file that a later start can load') and on cache-policy's decision starting-contents, not on this component's text;
    and it is counted during ordinary runs, not offline, at startup or in an opt-in profiling run as calibration says.
  responsibility_sha256: 42427be49ff601b5a5644394a2710dfbd0fcc13298c239a37f3144b0c0385dfe
  does: Inside the engine process, record what the run selected at start, count cache hits and storage reads per layer,
    and record how often each expert is routed, writing each when asked.
- component: server-metrics
  title: Request accounting and metric exporters
  described_in: comp/muse/server-metrics
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/server-metrics
  type: telemetry
  responsibility_sha256: f4211edbcc37eb1bf2dc711f407c89ce008b4bbb75f41c4e5aaa3a3e6e684f92
  does: In the server process, turn the engine's end-of-request figures and the server's own clocks into per-request records,
    running totals and a live rate, fill the usage and timings of each response, sample the machine at intervals, and render
    all of it for outside monitors.
types_without_a_part:
- type: graph-capture
  needed_when: The device benefits from pre-recorded or pre-compiled work, or first-use compilation would stall a request.
- type: device-backend
- type: secondary-compute
  needed_when: A second device can compute something sooner than moving its inputs to the main device, or has spare capacity
    the main device lacks.
- type: model-edit
  needed_when: The engine offers run-time changes to the model's behaviour.
- type: media-preparation
  needed_when: The engine serves input other than text.
- type: modality-encoding
  needed_when: The model accepts input other than text and the engine serves it.
- type: row-source
  needed_when: The model has a table too large to hold whole in fast memory, of which each token reads a few rows.
- type: storage-reader
  needed_when: Several kinds of data are read from the same storage while the engine runs.
- type: recurrent-state-store
  needed_when: The model has state that cannot be cut back to an earlier position, such as recurrent or convolution state.
- type: state-pool
  needed_when: Several sequences are in the engine at once and share one backing memory for state.
- type: state-tiering
  needed_when: State in fast memory exceeds what fits, for long contexts or many sequences.
- type: draft-proposal
  needed_when: 'A cheap source of proposals exists: a draft head of the model, a separate small model, or repetition in
    the text.'
- type: draft-policy
  needed_when: The amount of drafting is adjusted while running.
- type: draft-verification
  needed_when: Tokens are proposed ahead.
- type: output-constraint
  needed_when: The service offers constrained output, or a format that must be enforced.
- type: step-scheduler
- type: replica-routing
  needed_when: Several whole copies of the engine run side by side.
- type: scoring
  needed_when: The service offers scoring.
- type: model-partitioning
  needed_when: The model is spread over more than one device or machine.
- type: device-communication
  needed_when: The model is spread over more than one device or machine.
- type: resource-governing
  needed_when: 'What the engine may use changes while it runs: the system reclaims memory, sequences come and go, or power
    is limited.'
